nodes.name: Meta Leadgen Webhook
nodes.notes: GET and POST on ONE path because Meta needs both and registers only one callback URL: GET is the subscription handshake carrying hub.challenge, POST is every delivery. rawBody is ON and is not optional -- Meta signs the exact bytes it sent, and n8n parsing the JSON and handing on an object destroys them. With rawBody off, Verify Or Refuse answers 500 RAW_BODY_NOT_AVAILABLE on every delivery rather than failing open.

nodes.name: Verify Or Refuse
nodes.notes: Body kept in the repo at ops/n8n-meta-lead-ads/verify-and-extract.node.js and inserted here programmatically. Handles BOTH branches: the GET handshake (verdict CHALLENGE) and the POST HMAC check over the raw bytes. Nothing upstream or inside this node writes anything.

nodes.name: Signature Verified And Usable?
nodes.notes: ACCEPT only. CHALLENGE, ACCEPT_UNUSABLE, ACCEPT_NO_LEAD and REFUSE all take the false branch to Respond Without Writing, which answers with the status and text the Code node already decided -- including echoing hub.challenge back to Meta as plain text.

nodes.name: Respond Without Writing
nodes.notes: respondWith TEXT, not json: Meta's handshake requires the bare hub.challenge value as the body, and a JSON-quoted "31337" fails verification. The refusal paths reuse it and answer their reason_code as plain text, which is what the GO-LIVE probes measured.

nodes.name: Resolve Dealership From Page
nodes.notes: page_id is PUBLIC -- it is on the Page's About tab. It is safe to route on only because it arrived inside a body whose HMAC verified AND because it is registered here. The resolver is a three-way lock: an active identity, an active endpoint and an active dealership, or zero rows. alwaysOutputData is on so the zero-row case reaches its own branch instead of the workflow ending silently with Meta holding no answer.

nodes.name: Page Registered To A Dealership?
nodes.notes: Zero rows means this Facebook Page is not registered to any dealership, or its endpoint is still disabled. Both are configuration, not attack: the signature already verified.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ outcome: 'NOT_RECORDED', reason_code: 'PAGE_NOT_REGISTERED', why: 'The signature verified but this Facebook Page resolves to no active dealership endpoint. Register it in lead_ingest_provider_identity and enable the endpoint.', wrote_nothing: true }) }}

nodes.name: Respond Page Not Registered
nodes.notes: 500, not 4XX. A 4XX tells Meta not to retry and for a lead that means it is gone; this is our configuration gap and a redelivery after the row is registered still saves the customer.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_public_key: $json.public_key, p_external_event_id: $('Verify Or Refuse').item.json.leadgen_id, p_origin_verified: $('Verify Or Refuse').item.json.origin_verified, p_payload_raw: $('Verify Or Refuse').item.json.payload_raw, p_occurred_at: $('Verify Or Refuse').item.json.created_time, p_normalized: null }) }}

nodes.name: Record Lead Event
nodes.notes: p_normalized is NULL on purpose and that is what makes the row born RECEIVED rather than HYDRATED. Meta sent six identifiers and no customer, so there is nothing to normalize yet. SAFE to retry: the function is keyed on lead_event_identity_key (tenant_id, source_key, external_event_id) and returns was_duplicate = true for a redelivery rather than raising.

nodes.name: Fetch Lead From Graph
nodes.notes: Hop two. Resolves the dealership's own Page token from the vault keyed on page_id, then GET /v<v>/<leadgen_id> with an Authorization: Bearer header. The token is never in the URL, and Graph's error.message -- which echoes the request -- is never carried out. Body kept at ops/n8n-meta-lead-ads/fetch-lead-from-graph.node.js and inserted here programmatically.

nodes.name: Fetched?
nodes.notes: The false branch is NOT an error. It is the honest end of a lead whose customer could not be fetched: the lead_event row stays at RECEIVED, no leads row exists, and the reason_code names which of the six failures it was.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ outcome: 'RECEIVED_NOT_HYDRATED', reason_code: $json.reason_code, why: $json.why, event_id: $json.event_id, phase_remains: 'RECEIVED', retryable: $json.retryable }) }}

nodes.name: Respond Not Hydrated
nodes.notes: Status comes from the item, so the 200/500 decision stays in the Code node that holds the reasons instead of being re-derived here. 500 where a human can still fix it (no token, dead token, no Lead Access, rate limit); 200 where a retry can never succeed.

nodes.name: Normalize And Redact
nodes.notes: Hop three. Reads $input.first().json as the Graph response itself -- which is exactly what Fetch Lead From Graph emits -- and reads event_id from Record Lead Event, not from the gate, which never had one. Body kept at ops/n8n-meta-lead-ads/normalize-and-redact.node.js.

nodes.name: Hydrate Lead Event
nodes.notes: Refuses anything that is not phase RECEIVED (LEAD_EVENT_NOT_AWAITING_HYDRATION), which is what stops a redelivery overwriting a lead a salesperson is already working from. p_normalized is passed only when the shape is promotable -- a defective one is recorded as the defect it is by Reject Lead Event rather than stored as half a customer.

nodes.name: Can Promote?
nodes.notes: Read from Normalize And Redact, not from $json: the item here is the hydrate RPC's return value, which does not carry can_promote. nexus_lead_normalized_defect requires a full name and at least one of email or phone; a form that collected less is a fact about the form.

nodes.name: Promote Lead Event
nodes.notes: Creates the leads row and the audit_log row. Raises NX001 LEAD_EVENT_NOT_HYDRATED on a RECEIVED row, so a broken Graph hop can never produce a blank lead -- it produces a row that stops.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_event_id: $('Record Lead Event').item.json.event_id, p_phase: 'REJECTED', p_reason: 'The lead form did not collect enough to contact anyone: ' + $('Normalize And Redact').item.json.normalized_defect + '. The delivery and the Graph fetch were both fine - the form is what needs changing.' }) }}

nodes.name: Reject Lead Event
nodes.notes: REJECTED, with the promoter's own defect name in the reason. This is not an error path: it is a real lead whose form asked for too little, made visible as that rather than promoted and left to rot.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ outcome: 'PROMOTED', event_id: $('Record Lead Event').item.json.event_id, leadgen_id: $('Verify Or Refuse').item.json.leadgen_id, ad_platform: $('Normalize And Redact').item.json.ad_platform }) }}

nodes.name: Respond Promoted
nodes.notes: Meta is told 200 either way; what differs is what we recorded. No customer data is echoed back onto the wire.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ outcome: 'RECORDED_NOT_PROMOTED', event_id: $('Record Lead Event').item.json.event_id, normalized_defect: $('Normalize And Redact').item.json.normalized_defect }) }}

nodes.name: Respond Rejected
nodes.notes: 200: the delivery was fine and is recorded. Asking Meta to redeliver would change nothing, because the form will collect the same too-little next time.
